Amortized-analysis chapter

Amortized-analysis scientific and visual review

Delivery status

Quality-reviewed English draft; student approval is not inferred. The chapter contains twenty teaching sections, a complete-sentence summary, 87 worked problem entries, 80 final reasoning rules and twenty specialized exact-cost models. Two problem entries are explicitly revisited authentic examination bridges, not newly discovered unique archive questions. Five university lectures were actually read; four form the core synthesis.

Mathematical review

The review independently checked 9334 inputs, 294906 checkpoints and 10869 result contracts. These include every increment count in a bounded set for all starting states of counters of widths two through six, all append/pop sequences through length nine, all enqueue/dequeue patterns through length eight, and all ternary-valued monotonic inputs through length seven with both equality policies. Counter work was computed from independent integer XOR transitions. Monotonic survivors were computed from suffix dominance rather than by replaying a stack. Sorted-block work was computed from construction frequency by level. Every completed simulated operation satisfied the full telescoping identity.

The textual review checks exact power-of-two endpoints, initial capacity, nonzero starting potential, modulo overflow, weighted costs, clipped growth potentials, integer ceilings, minimum-capacity and midpoint cases, post-delete versus pre-delete shrinking, queue order, persistent branching, and allocation limitations. Big-O expressions are not canceled as if their hidden constants were equal. Expected hashing assumptions remain distinct from deterministic visit counts. The intentionally bad half-shrink example is labeled as a counterexample.

Problem review

The 85 original/reconstructed problems cover numerical sums, complete endpoint calculations, coefficient derivations, adversarial sequences, weighted models, counterexample construction and representation contracts. Solutions state how the result follows and why an attractive alternative fails. Original PhD CE 1404 Q9 and MSc CE 1405 Q56 were rendered and visually re-read. Their independent English adaptations preserve printed alternatives, source paths and content hashes. No official answer key is claimed.

Visual companions are attached when an actual transition trace clarifies the argument. Their named sample inputs are scoped explicitly when a question uses larger or symbolic data. Pure algebra and quantifier questions use a complete written certificate instead of an unrelated moving diagram. The visual-decision ledger records this distinction for every problem.

Browser review

The dedicated real Edge run covers every one of 691 stored checkpoints across twenty unique models. It checks plot bounds, label padding and overlap, unique moving record identifiers, loaded fonts, native mathematics, actual geometric movement, pause/resume, before/after comparison, previous/next, seeking, restart, reduced motion, print checkpoints, editable parameter boundaries and invalid-input preservation. It also checks mobile overflow, the chapter-library entry and the week-four link. Browser evidence records the latest result rather than treating screenshot generation alone as a pass.

Mathematics uses native MathML and STIX Two Math. Headings use Newsreader, prose uses Source Sans 3 and code uses JetBrains Mono. The diagrams remain within a 760 by 400 view box; storage indices and record identifiers have separate labels. Counter bits, old/new array buffers, input/output queue stacks, monotonic candidates, binary-sized sorted blocks and migration routing use distinct readings and state representations. Formula charges are evaluated only at completed operation endpoints. During partial array operations the displayed potential is explicitly the last completed potential; counter popcount tracks each real flip.

Retention and uncertainty

All 55 preceding chapter HTML files are retained byte for byte. The library now has 56 chapter entries and 3826 worked problem entries. Publication status is tracked separately from local and GitHub source completeness.

This finite audit supports the declared mathematical models; it is not a formal verification of every production implementation. Allocation, nonconstant payload moves, concurrent mutation and persistent sharing need the contracts described in the lesson. The source pool is bounded, inaccessible lecture candidates are not counted as read, and the exercise bank does not claim to reproduce every copyrighted exercise of every course. There is no literal 100-percent accuracy or unseen-question performance guarantee. Remaining uncertainty is reported rather than concealed.
